reason: Gelatin is commonly derived from pork or non-zabiha beef/cattle bones and skin. Source must be explicitly confirmed as halal-certified (fish or halal-slaughtered bovine) before use.
Ethanol/drinking alcohol is haram to consume in Islamic dietary law.
Wine is an alcoholic beverage and is haram, including as a cooking ingredient (deglazing, reductions, marinades).
Beer is an alcoholic beverage and is haram, including as a cooking ingredient (batters, braises).
Distilled spirits (rum, whiskey, brandy, etc.) are haram alcohol.
Rum is a distilled alcoholic spirit and is haram.
Standard vanilla extract is suspended in ethanol (35%+ alcohol by volume). Requires an alcohol-free/food-grade halal-certified alternative.
Flavor extracts (vanilla, almond, lemon, etc.) are frequently alcohol-based carriers. Verify the specific extract is alcohol-free.
Lard is rendered pork fat and is haram.
Pork and all pork derivatives are haram.
Bacon is a pork product and is haram.
Ham is a pork product and is haram.
Pepperoni is traditionally made from pork (and sometimes beef); source must be confirmed halal-certified beef/turkey to be acceptable.
Chicken must be zabiha (Islamically slaughtered) to be halal. Without an explicit halal-sourcing note, mainstream commercial chicken cannot be assumed halal.
Beef must be from a zabiha-slaughtered, halal-certified source. Without an explicit halal-sourcing note, it cannot be assumed halal.
Lamb must be from a zabiha-slaughtered, halal-certified source. Without an explicit halal-sourcing note, it cannot be assumed halal.
Turkey must be from a zabiha-slaughtered, halal-certified source. Without an explicit halal-sourcing note, it cannot be assumed halal.
Generic 'meat' ingredient with no species or sourcing note cannot be verified as halal-slaughtered.
Sausage casings and fillers can include pork or non-halal meat/gelatin binders unless explicitly halal-certified.
E120 (carmine/cochineal) is derived from crushed insects; considered haram/mashbooh by most scholars, commonly treated as impermissible.
Carmine (E120) is an insect-derived colorant considered haram/mashbooh by most scholars.
Cochineal (source of E120/carmine) is an insect-derived colorant considered haram/mashbooh by most scholars.
E441 is gelatin; source (pork vs. halal-certified bovine/fish) must be verified.
E471 (mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids) can be sourced from animal or plant fat; source must be verified as halal/plant-based.
Emulsifiers of this type can be animal-derived (including pork fat); source must be verified.
Animal rennet (used in cheese-making) is often derived from non-zabiha slaughtered animals; microbial/plant/halal-certified rennet is required.
Whey can be produced using animal rennet from non-halal-slaughtered animals; verify halal certification.
E920/L-cysteine (used as a dough conditioner) is sometimes derived from human hair or animal feathers/pork; synthetic or plant source must be confirmed.
Traditional mirin contains alcohol; requires an alcohol-free version.
Cooking wine is an alcoholic ingredient and is haram.
Marshmallows typically contain gelatin from an unverified (often pork) source.
Gummy candies typically contain gelatin from an unverified (often pork) source.
